svg.title: Three ways to train a pilot, and the script pull
svg.desc: Three ways to train a pilot. Used in this order when used together. A run may use one, two or all three. Three numbered boxes are joined by down arrows. Step 1, Copy the script. The entries call it behaviour cloning, BC. Record the script, the hand-written pilot, flying many matches. Train the network to pick the same action the script picked at each moment. An outlined azure ship follows a dashed track beside a stack of recorded moments. Step 2, Let the copy fly, and correct it. The entries call it DAgger. The copy flies on its own and drifts into situations the script never got into. At each one the script says what it would have done there. The copy trains on those answers too. A filled azure ship drifts off a dashed straight track. Thin arrows point back toward the straight track, showing what the script would have done. Step 3, Trial and error. The entries call it PPO. The pilot plays many matches and earns points for good outcomes, such as damage dealt and wins, and loses some for bad ones. After each batch it is adjusted to do more of what earned points. One round is an update. A dashed circle with three arrowheads joins play, points and adjust in a repeating cycle. The script pull, during trial and error. The entries also say teacher. One moment is shown. The pilot's odds for one control are three azure bars labelled left, straight and right, with left tallest. The script's choice for the same moment is one outlined bar labelled right. A thick arrow labelled pull points from the pilot's bars toward the script's choice. An extra term in the adjustment pulls the pilot's choices toward the script's. It acts only on some moments of training, and its strength fades over the run, to nothing. A strip labelled moments of training has some squares filled azure, with the key pulled. Which moments, and how strongly, changed from run to run.
